decisions.rationale: In the title, breast cancer modifies the noun susceptibility (breast cancer-susceptibility), so it is a disease mention used as a modifier of another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: Autosomal recessive disorder refers to a family of multiple genetically inherited diseases rather than one specific disease definition.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Disease Class (autosomal recessive disease example)

decisions.rationale: Ataxia-telangiectasia is a single named disease with one specific definition and no further categorization.
A-T is the abbreviation of ataxia-telangiectasia and is annotated as a separate synonymous mention referring to the same specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 6: Synonymous mentions (abbreviations annotated separately)

decisions.rationale: Breast cancer as the object of the phrase risk for refers to the disease itself and does not modify another noun phrase.
Patients with breast cancer refers to a specific disease; breast cancer is the head of the mention rather than a modifier.
Sporadic breast cancer refers to a specific disease mention; the qualifier sporadic does not form a separate disease category and the span is kept as given.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Specific Disease and 5: Minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: Breast cancer developed at age under 45 refers to a specific disease experienced by the patients.
Breast tumor refers to a specific tumor disease diagnosed in the patients; tumor is explicitly retained as a disease term and is not a general term.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4: General terms (cancer and tumor are retained)

decisions.rationale: Bilateral breast cancer refers to a specific disease in the patients, and breast cancer is the disease mention itself.
In the hyphenated phrase A-T disease-causing, A-T disease modifies the noun mutations, so it is a disease mention used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: Risk of breast cancer in heterozygotes refers to the disease itself as the object of risk and is not modifying another concept.
A type of breast cancer characterized by bilateral occurrence refers to breast cancer as a disease, consistently annotated as a specific disease mention like the other breast cancer mentions.
